items.defectStatement: TopicsController#unsubscribe changes and saves the logged-in user's topic notification level on an unauthenticated-by-CSRF GET. A cross-site navigation carrying the user's session can therefore change that preference without their consent.
obligations: Prevent ordinary cross-site GET requests from changing notification preferences.
Require a CSRF-protected submission or a validated authorization token bound to the intended user and topic.
Keep a working unsubscribe flow from email links and preserve topic access checks.
Preserve the existing notification-level transitions for authorized requests.
items.notes: Routes currently expose only GET for this action. A protected submission requires coordinated routing and caller changes; signed links require token generation too. Merely rejecting GET disables the feature, and Rails' normal CSRF verification exempts GET.

items.defectStatement: The client unsubscribe route loads ordinary topic data without invoking the unsubscribe action. An in-app transition therefore displays the unsubscribe message while leaving the user's notification preference unchanged.
obligations: Invoke the unsubscribe operation on an in-app transition before resolving the model successfully.
Populate and return the topic model from the resulting topic JSON.
Reuse server-preloaded unsubscribe results without applying the notification-level change twice.
Propagate request failures instead of displaying success.
items.notes: The frozen input omits the endpoint contract and PreloadStore API. This example uses the existing GET endpoint and fixes this finding independently of #01. An unconditional unsubscribe request would apply a second downgrade after a full-page request.

items.defectStatement: TopicsController#unsubscribe assumes TopicUser.find_by returns a record and immediately reads its notification_level. When the user has no topic_users row for the topic, the action raises NoMethodError instead of saving an unsubscribe preference.
obligations: Provide a usable TopicUser record when the lookup finds none.
Associate any new record with the current user and requested topic.
Persist the unsubscribe preference through the existing save and preserve transitions for existing records.
items.exampleFix:
tu = TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])
    tu.notification_level ||= TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]

    if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
items.notes: TopicUser.get also delegates to find_by and can return nil; replacing only the helper name is insufficient. A new record starts at regular and is muted by the existing branch.
